parts.text:
19 A sailboat is pushed by the wind at a constant velocity v across a lake.
The force of the wind and the velocity of the sailboat are in the same direction.
Which additional information is required to determine the work done per unit time by the wind
acting on the sailboat?
A
the force exerted by the wind
B
the distance travelled by the sailboat per unit time
C
the total energy input to the sailboat by the wind
D
the weight of the sailboat

hints: Notice the phrase work done per unit time - this is the definition of power $P$ measured in $\text{W}$.
Recall that for a force parallel to velocity, power is $P = Fv$, and the question states wind force and velocity $v$ are in the same direction.
Since $v$ is already given, identify which missing quantity in $P = Fv$ would let you complete the calculation.
walkthrough: Identify the target quantity: work done per unit time by the wind is power $P$.
State the governing rule: for force $F$ in the same direction as velocity $v$, $P = Fv$.
Check what is known: the sailboat moves at constant velocity $v$, so $v$ is known but $F$ is not.
Conclude that the wind force $F$ is the extra information needed to calculate $P = Fv$.

A.explanation: With velocity $v$ known, knowing the wind force $F$ allows power to be found from $P = Fv$.

B.explanation: Distance per unit time is speed, which is already given as $v$, so it adds no new information.

C.explanation: Total energy input without the time taken does not give energy per unit time.

D.explanation: Weight acts vertically while motion is horizontal, so it does not determine the wind's power.
